title: Student-built AI flags listless and feverish lion-head geese; Shantou cooperative reports 30% higher survival
summary: Sixteen Shenzhen University students with Tencent engineers built a camera system from 6,000 labeled images; Xinhua (13 Oct 2023) reports real-time alerts and 30% higher survival at the cooperative.
account: Xinhua reported on 13 October 2023 (syndicated by CGTN the next day) that a team of 16 students from the Shenzhen University-Tencent Cloud AI BEng program, invited in 2022 by goose farmer Jin Shutao to his lion-head goose cooperative in Houxi Village, Chenghai District, Shantou, built an AI program that identifies sick geese by measuring how long each bird stays still, supplemented by detecting feverish goslings. Working in a 500 m² space holding over 4,000 geese, they used existing farm cameras, manually labeled 6,000 images of 300,000 geese, and with Tencent engineers improved recognition in crowded scenes and tracking of each goose's stillness. The program now gives real-time alerts for 'listless geese' and 'feverish geese' and displays temperature, humidity and PM2.5 trends; Xinhua states this has helped the farm increase survival of lion-head geese by 30 percent, quoting student Wang Yifeng and Shen Linlin of Shenzhen University's visual research institute. The article recalls a 2018 avian influenza outbreak that left five of thousands of geese in the village alive. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the event (2023-10-13-d63c). The 30% figure is undated and unsupported by method, so the date is the report's.
purpose: Identify sick geese from camera footage by how long they stay still (and fever in goslings) and alert breeders in real time.
system: AI goose-breeding program (recognition and tracking algorithms on farm cameras)
developer: Sixteen students of the Shenzhen University-Tencent Cloud AI BEng program, guided by university teachers and Tencent engineers
deployer: Jin Shutao's lion-head goose farming cooperative, Houxi Village, Chenghai District, Shantou
taxonomy_note: Benefit created on an identifiable system, farm and reported outcome, but the 30% survival gain rests on state-media reports with no baseline, period or method, so the organizational depth is set conservatively. Listed in the OECD AI Incidents Monitor; the parent workflow classed it as an aggregate benefit.

ratings.reason: Xinhua states the program 'has helped the farm increase the survival rate of lion-head geese by 30 percent'; no baseline, period or verification is given.
Farmer Jin Shutao is named but no personal outcome beyond the farm figure is reported.

ai_role.statement: The system's real-time alerts are the only mechanism described for the survival gain; the reports do not separate the AI's effect from other changes on the farm. Sources are independent news reports (Xinhua, CGTN) with named sources; no veterinary or peer-reviewed confirmation was found.
